text:
elaine: quick follow-up from yesterday's rfc review — i still have questions about the streaming request lifecycle at the edge. do we want the edge to hold a tiny resume token for soft-resume semantics, or should we force clients to re-open from scratch on any disconnect?

jordan: leaning toward lightweight resume token. avoids redoing KV-cache priming and gives better UX for long lived streams.

samir: agree on UX but worried about memory and tenant accounting. how long do we keep tokens? LRU + short TTL?

elaine: proposal: keep resume token for 30s after connection close, constant O(1) metadata per stream (token, last-offset, model-variant). evict on memory pressure.

alyssa: 30s seems fine for mobile flakey networks. what about billing and duplicate tokens? if client retries, we might double bill.

jordan: we can attach a short-idempotency id to the token so retry within TTL maps to same billing checkpoint. basically: `Resume-Token` + `Resume-Idempotency` header.

samir: small nit: idempotency needs to carry side-effect semantics. for non-idempotent requests (tool-calls) we might need to mark token as "no-resume" and force fresh execution.

elaine: yep — contract: resume allowed only if request metadata is resume-safe. we should have an explicit header `Edge-Resume-Safe: true|false`. default false.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: edge-resume-feature toggle -> staging at 2024-11-10T03:00Z :wrench:

alyssa: observability concern: we need clear traces showing resume hits/misses, token evictions, and billing dedupe decisions. otherwise postmortems will be painful.

jordan: agree. logs: `resume_attempt`, `resume_hit`, `resume_evicted`, `resume_conflict(billing)` — include tenant_id, route, model_variant, last_offset.

samir: prefer structured trailers for client-visible progress when we resume. e.g., send trailers like: `Resume-Status: resumed|stale|none` and `Resume-Offset: 12345`

elaine: implementation questions: do we buffer any streaming tokens server-side to re-send missed tokens, or is client responsible for diffing? i'd rather avoid buffering large payloads.

jordan: avoid buffering. edge should only persist tiny metadata and rely on client to re-request missing tokens/segments. if we need server-side replay for small deltas we can add short-lived KV snapshots later.

alyssa: what about backpressure? if we resume and the downstream hw has advanced (kv cache warmed differently), we need to ensure we don't break latency SLOs. maybe resume should be best-effort and degrade to full restart if mismatch detected.

samir: yes — define a resume acceptance check: model_variant_id + last_kv_hash == current -> resume allowed. otherwise return `Resume-Status: stale` and instruct client to restart.

elaine: handshake example for client:
```
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Resume-Token: abc123
Resume-Idempotency: rxyz-987
Edge-Resume-Safe: true
```
edge reply on accept: trailers include `Resume-Status: resumed` and `Resume-Offset: 1024`

jordan: sounds good. small UX ask: expose a simple SDK primitive `stream.resumeIfPossible()` so customers don't have to manage headers directly.

alyssa: ok but we need to guard credential/permission semantics: resume tokens must be bound to the same auth context. no cross-tenant reuse.

samir: security checklist item added. token must be HMAC'd with tenant key and include expiry.

elaine: next steps:
- write short RFC addendum with handshake examples and `Edge-Resume-Safe` contract (i'll draft)
- add resume telemetry events to console + billing dedupe story (jordan/alyssa)
- design token store memory bounds and TTL eviction (samir)

jordan: i'll mock up the console dashboard tiles for resume rate, evictions, and billing conflicts.

samir: i'll propose memory budget and a per-edge-shard token cap.

elaine: thanks — tagging owners: @jordan @samir @alyssa. tl;dr: lightweight resume tokens, short TTL, resume-safe contract, telemetry + billing dedupe, fallback-to-restart on mismatch.

ops-bot: reminder: RFC addendum draft PR required before feature toggle to staging (link: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/pull/456)

jordan: i'll put a draft PR by EOD. :+1:

elaine: great. if no blockers i'll lock these decisions into the addendum tonight.
